_comment: Per-order quantity limits used by the automatic order-splitting engine.
These are the FALLBACK values: the broker limit resolver first asks the
broker adapter for live limits (fetch_order_limits) and only uses this file
when the broker does not expose them. Adding a new broker requires nothing
here unless it deviates — never a change to the execution engine.
Lookup order: <broker>.<UNDERLYING> -> <broker>.* -> exchange.<UNDERLYING>
-> exchange.* -> default.*
The freeze quantities live under "exchange" because that is what they are:
an NSE/BSE/MCX property of the CONTRACT, identical whichever broker routes
the order. They used to be duplicated into the angel and icici blocks and
omitted from kotak and dhan, which left those two with no cap at all — so a
Kotak-only or Dhan-only user's oversized order was sent whole for the
exchange to reject, with an opaque broker error instead of a clear one.
supportsSplitting is a property of CHARTICKS, not of the broker: splitting is
several ordinary orders sent in sequence (OrderManager._place_with_splitting),
so every broker supports it. A broker block may still set it false to opt out.
maxLotsPerOrder / maxQtyPerOrder may be null (= no cap on that dimension);
when both are null, or supportsSplitting is false, the order is sent whole.
VERIFY these against the current NSE / BSE / MCX freeze-quantity circular
before relying on them — the exchanges revise them, and a stale value here
means orders split into children the exchange still rejects.
